definitions.gloss: samurai residence; the mansion or estate of a warrior-class family, especially during the Edo period
definitions.explanation: samurai residence; the mansion or estate of a warrior-class family, especially during the Edo period

examples.japanese: {武家屋敷|ぶけやしき}を{見学|けんがく}する。
この{通|とお}りには{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}の{武家屋敷|ぶけやしき}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Edo-period samurai residences remain along this street.

examples.japanese: {角館|かくのだて}の{武家屋敷|ぶけやしき}{通|どお}りは{桜|さくら}の{名所|めいしょ}としても{知|し}られている。
examples.english: The samurai residence street in Kakunodate is also famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot.

notes:
Refers to the residential compounds of samurai families, particularly those from the Edo period (1603–1868). During that era, {武家屋敷|ぶけやしき} were arranged around the lord's castle according to rank, with higher-ranking samurai living closer to the castle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {武家屋敷|ぶけやしき}{通|どお}り — samurai residence street
- {武家屋敷|ぶけやしき}{群|ぐん} — cluster of samurai residences
- {武家屋敷|ぶけやしき}{跡|あと} — site of a former samurai residence

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many cities preserve samurai districts as tourist attractions, including {角館|かくのだて} (Akita), {長町|ながまち} (Kanazawa), and {知覧|ちらん} (Kagoshima). These preserved neighborhoods give visitors a sense of Edo-period urban planning and samurai lifestyle.

RELATED WORDS:
- {武家|ぶけ} — warrior class; samurai family
- {屋敷|やしき} — mansion; estate
- {城下町|じょうかまち} — castle town
